title: 'What is Brick mode?': before/after lock screen explainer
attribution_visible_in_image: Visible: headline 'What is Brick mode?'; 'BRICK' device mark inside the lock screen widget. No creator credit visible.
contains_third_party_content: App icons (YouTube, TikTok, Instagram, Spotify) and photographed hands/devices.

observed.layout: Bold black headline 'What is Brick mode?' over a light background; two hand-held phones labeled 'Bricked' and 'Unbricked' separated by 'vs.'. Bricked: date, large time 9:41, a wide widget with a BRICK device icon and a running timer (9:10:55), weather advisory text, a small alarm chip (7:35 AM), a Spotify chip, flashlight and camera buttons. Unbricked: the same date and time plus a 'Notification Center' list with YouTube (3), TikTok (4) and Instagram (2) notification groups.
observed.hierarchy: Headline, then the two phones; the message is the contrast between empty space and a notification stack.
observed.typography: Heavy tight display sans for the headline; system-style UI inside phones.
observed.iconography: Brand app icons and system glyphs.

interpretation.concept: A subtractive mode: removing information to reduce distraction, proven by symmetric before/after framing.
implementation_notes: Two identical frames, same scale and background, label above each.
Lock-screen UI composited on device mockups with hands.

concept_work.essence: Make a mode understandable at a glance by holding everything constant except the thing that changes.
what_makes_it_work: Identical framing isolates the one variable.
gaps_to_make_it_work: Third-party app logos and photographed hands complicate reuse.
The Bricked screen's widgets are small; the benefit is shown by emptiness, not explained.

pattern.name: Symmetric before/after state comparison
use_when: Explaining a mode, setting or redesign
avoid_when: Differences are subtle and need annotation
must_preserve: Same frame, scale and background for both states
adaptation_examples: Dark-mode explainer: same frame, light vs dark UI.
Pricing: Free vs Pro as equal cards.

lessons: Hold everything constant except the variable you want to show.
Let empty space carry the argument when the concept is subtraction.

measured.palette_method: Median-cut quantization of the supplied image plus saturated-pixel hue medians. Approximate (JPEG). Items marked 'approx' were judged by eye.
palette: skin tones from the hand photos (~14%)
measured.color_roles: Neutral stage and black phones; the only color comes from app icons and hands.
measured.contrast_method: Estimated from the compressed image: background = dominant color in the measured box, foreground = mean of the most distant ~4% of pixels, ratio = WCAG relative-luminance contrast. Thin or anti-aliased text biases toward lower ratios; values within 0.3 of a threshold (3.0 or 4.5) are marked near_threshold and should be verified in the source file.

purpose.evidence: The single message (what the mode changes) is obvious in seconds.

visual.evidence: Strong headline, symmetric composition and ample space.

discipline.evidence: Comparison graphics are done correctly: equal frames, named states.

usability.evidence: The difference is legible without interaction; no explanation of how the mode is entered.

consistency.evidence: Consistent device framing, label style and spacing.

originality.evidence: Before/after is a standard explainer pattern; subtraction as the message is clear but familiar.

evidence: primary text min 17.85:1; secondary text min 14.55:1; icon min n/a:1; non-color state cue: True.
accessibility.basis: computed from measured contrast + cue flag (scope: contrast and non-color cues only; touch targets, motion, screen-reader support are not assessable from a static image)

evaluation.readiness_key: A = ship with minor adjustments (>=80, no critical failure); B = needs specific fixes (60-79); C = rethink (<60)
evaluation.scope: Scored as presented in a static image. States, motion and behavior that are not shown are not scored as present.
